title: Croatia vs England: Stadium Nearly Full Despite UEFA Sanction
seoTitle: Croatia vs England: Rijeka Stadium Nearly Full Despite.
subtitle: Croatian Federation Uses Regulatory Exception to Fill Rijeka Stands
excerpt: Despite UEFA's decision to close the gates, the match between Croatia and England will have about 75% of the stands occupied thanks to a loophole in the rules.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Croatia and England, scheduled for this Saturday in Rijeka, has gained prominence because, despite UEFA's sanction that determined closed gates, the stadium is expected to host almost 75% of its capacity. The exception used by the Croatian federation allows spectators to enter under specific conditions.

UEFA's Sanction and the Regulatory Loophole

The Croatian Federation was sanctioned after incidents involving fans in the last Nations League against France, when seven fans were detained on suspicion of Nazi salutes. UEFA mandated that the match against England be played behind closed doors and prohibited Croatian fans from attending the clash against the Czech Republic.

How the Children's Exception Works

UEFA regulations stipulate that children up to 14 years old can attend behind-closed-doors matches without payment, provided they are accompanied by an adult. The required ratio is one adult for every fifteen children, and the minors must be affiliated with schools or football academies in the country. This clause allows Rijeka Stadium, with a capacity of 8,279 people, to host up to 6,000 spectators.

Who Can Enter the Stadium

In addition to the children and accompanying adults, the exception authorizes the presence of 100 English fans in the designated visitor section. VIP guests from both national teams, team delegations, and media, security, infrastructure, and UEFA organization professionals can also occupy the stadium.

Expectations for the Croatia vs England Clash

The match, which takes place at 1 PM (Brasília time) in the third round of Group 3 of Nations League A, will be broadcast live on Sportv, with real-time coverage by the ge portal. The presence of a crowd, even if limited, could influence the game's atmosphere and generate additional interest among fans who followed UEFA's decision.
